Hi Marta — thanks for the clear list, and looping in our security and contracts leads (Irene and Lauren) so we can get you a concise package. Quick summary answers below and I attached a term sheet to align on. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if you want to run through.

Answers (high-level):
- Key management: Yes — for Azure Private we support BYOK via customer-managed Azure Key Vaults. You can provision HSM-backed keys and we never hold plaintext keys. We also support integration with Azure Dedicated HSM where required.
- Data residency & logs: Customer data remains in your Azure subscription/region. We provide a streaming audit log to your chosen storage account; default retention is 365 days but we can extend retention for enterprise customers. Logs are exportable in JSON/CSV.
- SOC2: SOC2 Type II report available; attaching a redacted copy for your review.
- IP escrow / continuity: Redwood does not escrow third-party proprietary model weights (we do not control customer-owned or third-party model IP). For operational continuity we offer an "Emergency Continuity Package" as part of our enterprise private agreements:
  * Delivery of deployment artifacts (containerized runtime, orchestration manifests) into escrow
  * A limited emergency license to run the last-approved runtime in the event Redwood is unable to operate the service
  * Runbooks and engineering handover materials
  * Escrow activation requires a signed enterprise addendum and a one-time escrow administration fee

We attached: Redwood_PrivatePlan_TermSheet_v1.pdf (commercial + continuity options) and SOC2_TypeII_redacted.pdf.

Proposed next step: quick legal/technical call tomorrow to walk the redlines and confirm the escrow scope. Suggested times: 10:00am or 2:00pm PT.

Hi Marta — a few technical clarifications from security to make sure the term sheet addresses your team's expectations: 

- KMS details: We integrate with customer-managed Azure Key Vaults (RBAC and Managed Identities). Keys never leave the vault and all encryption/decryption calls occur within the customer's VNet when the private deployment is used. We support Azure Key Vault HSM-protected keys for FIPS compliance.
- Auditing: Audit events (request metadata, token-level usage) are streamed to customer storage; default retention is 365 days, can be extended to 3 years with an add-on. We can provide a monthly logs export to your SIEM via Event Hub.
- Escrow artifacts: the artifacts that can be escrowed are our runtime images, deployment manifests, and approved configuration templates. We cannot escrow third-party closed-source model weights or any data that contains customer PII. For open-source model checkpoints (OSS licenses that permit redistribution) we can include reproducible build artifacts where licensing allows.

I'll share a short playbook that maps these items into contract language for your counsel to consider.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Security Lead, Redwood Inference

Carlos / Marta — appreciate the clarity and the redlines. Quick summary of Redwood's position and a proposed compromise that I will escalate to our legal ops: 

- Model weights escrow: Redwood cannot escrow third-party proprietary model weights or customer-provided model artifacts that violate downstream licenses. That said, for this private plan we will offer the following compromise (Enterprise addendum):
  * For open-source model checkpoints (permitted by license) we will include reproducible build artifacts and checksums in escrow.
  * For proprietary models used in Cusco's production workloads, Redwood will provide a frozen runtime image, deployment manifests, and documented migration runbook sufficient for an accredited third-party engineering team to run the last-approved model under a limited emergency license. We will also include a list of model dependencies and verified reproducibility steps where available.

- SLA & termination assistance: we can commit to defined SLA credit bands in the enterprise SOW (availability / P50 latency bands). We'll also include a 90-day termination assistance package (engineering support hours + runbook handover) as part of the Enterprise SOW; exact hours and rates to be captured in the SOW.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Lauren: can you pick up the attached Cusco redlines (we've flagged the IP/escrow and SLA clauses) and propose contract language that captures the compromise above?
2) Irene: can you confirm the exact artifacts we would put in escrow and any restrictions we need to call out for PII/PHI?
3) Marta/Carlos: if acceptable, we can update the DocuSign bundle and aim to get countersigned next week.
